name: Dry Arabia
summary: The standard open land map: no cliffs, water or elevation, even resources, three sacred sites between the players.
tips: Nothing blocks an early rush, so scout for feudal aggression and keep a tower or spears ready.
The three sacred sites sit between you and the enemy; whoever holds the middle can force fights there.
Trade posts are on the map edges, mirrored; check which side is safer for a trade route.

name: Gorge
summary: Open like Dry Arabia, but you start at the back of a gorge with a narrow choke in the centre and sacred sites on the raised sides.
tips: The central choke is easy to wall or tower, which slows feudal pressure.
Two sacred sites sit on the high ground beside the choke; ranged units there shoot down at anyone below.
Trade posts are near the middle of the edges, so trade routes are short and exposed.

name: Flankwoods
summary: Two lanes of stealth forest along the edges and a cliff-ringed plateau in the middle that holds both sacred sites, the trade post and most relics.
tips: Almost every objective is on the central plateau, so map control there decides the game.
Stealth forest on the flanks hides raids; keep vision on the forest lanes near your base.
Plan your first expansion toward the plateau rather than the edges.

name: Himeyama
summary: Each player starts on a hill above a central pond with a few fish; gold and stone are scarce and come in small deposits.
tips: You'll run out of starting gold and stone early, so take a second deposit in the valley before you need it.
The two sacred sites by the pond are heavily contested; plan a castle-age army to hold one.
The pond's fish are few, so a dock gives a small early boost but not a fishing economy.

name: West Lake
summary: A Yue Fei's Legacy map built around a lake.
tips: Scout the lake shore early to see whether a dock is worth it on this generation.

name: King of the Hill
summary: Two rings of cliffs form a central mountain with most of the gold and stone, several relics and a single sacred site that starts the victory timer at once.
tips: The centre sacred site is a win condition: if they hold it, you must take it back before the timer ends.
No trade posts, so the central gold is the long-game income. Contest the hill.
The forest band on the edges makes it easy to wall between the cliff and the map edge.

name: Hidden Valley
summary: Players start in depressions on opposite sides of a cliff-lined valley whose entrances are blocked by forest.
tips: The valley opens only as wood is chopped, so early rushes take longer to arrive.
One sacred site is in the valley and two sit beside it on the cliff edges; ranged units on the cliffs control the valley.
Relics are on the raised centre, not evenly split, so scout both sides.

name: Atacama
summary: Players ring a large central forest; outside it, wood is very scarce and you start with only a couple of small woodlines.
tips: Plan for wood: your starting woodlines run out fast and the big forest is in the middle, toward the enemy.
Expect fights near the central forest, where everyone ends up chopping.
You start with deer under your town center, so food is easy early.

name: Relic River
summary: A shallow river with waterfalls runs down the middle; every relic and sacred site is on its banks.
tips: All relics and sacred sites are at the river, so it is where the game is fought.
Land and ships can both move in the shallow river, but not over the waterfalls.
A dock can block the narrow river to enemy ships.

name: Hill and Dale
summary: The standard closed map: you start on a plateau with a few easy-to-wall entrances; the valley holds the sacred sites, trade posts, relics and extra resources.
tips: Walling your entrances is cheap here, so booms and fast castle are strong.
Everything worth taking is in the valley; expect the game to be decided there.
If they wall, don't waste units on the walls early. Out-eco them and take the centre.

name: Golden Heights
summary: A raised 'heights' area with extra gold, a small lake in one corner, and a single trade post in the west corner.
tips: Extra gold favours gold-heavy armies and long games.
Only one trade post, so trade is a smaller part of the game.
In 1v1 you start fairly close together next to the cliff, so expect early contact.

name: High View
summary: Lots of stealth forest across the map; you start on a gentle hill in a clearing.
tips: Stealth forest hides armies and raids; scout and keep units near your gold.
Wood is plentiful, so archer and wooden-unit play is cheap.
Sacred sites and trade posts run along the middle line between players.

name: Carmel
summary: Like Lipany with smaller cliffs; resources and features are clustered in the centre and the edges are empty.
tips: Gold is scarce, so take the central gold before they do.
Players spawn in opposite corners and the two sacred sites sit in the other corners.
Open map: guard against early aggression.

name: Lipany
summary: Dry Arabia with random cliffs and a lot of extra berries.
tips: Extra berries help civs with berry bonuses (Abbasid, Delhi, Byzantines).
Cliffs can block parts of the map and make walling easier; scout them before planning a rush.
Otherwise play it like Dry Arabia.

name: Hideout
summary: A ring of forest in the middle with stealth forest inside; players start in alcoves and the edges are rich in resources.
tips: In 1v1 you start far apart, so rushes are slow and booms are strong.
Sacred sites and trade posts are near opposite corners, away from the centre.
Rich edges mean you can expand safely behind you.

name: Mongolian Heights
summary: A river splits the map with five shallow crossings; each side gets one sacred site and one trade post.
tips: The five crossings are the chokes: watch them and fight there.
Each side has its own sacred site and trade post, so hold yours and raid theirs.
There's one extra relic, split evenly between sides.

name: The Pit
summary: A central valley flanked by cliffs splits the middle into three parts, each with a sacred site; trade posts are in two corners.
tips: All relics are in the centre sections, so contest the middle.
The valley sacred site is ringed by stealth forest; expect ambushes there.
Corner hills are reached from the side only, which makes them easy to hold.

name: Baltic
summary: Teams start on opposite sides of a sea; land is connected but far, so pressure from the water is faster.
tips: Get docks and fishing boats up early; the water decides most games.
Your town center is near the shore, so enemy ships can hit your base. Defend the coast.
Land armies take a long route, so naval pressure arrives first.

name: Rocky River
summary: A dried riverbed full of resources runs through the middle, between two fairly empty starting areas.
tips: The riverbed holds the resources and the middle sacred site, so fights happen there.
Wood is short in your base; plan early expansion toward the river's forests.
The two side sacred sites sit just outside the riverbed, one per side.

name: Oasis
summary: Teams start on opposite sides of a central oasis ringed by forest; outside that ring there's very little wood.
tips: Most wood is in the forest ring around the oasis, toward the middle.
Sacred sites spawn outside the oasis, between the teams.
Trade posts can spawn behind or between teams; check before you invest in traders.

name: Sunkenlands
summary: An open map like Dry Arabia with more random starts in craters and extra food; trade posts sit along the centre line.
tips: Extra food favours a fast boom.
Only two sacred sites, and the trade posts are in the middle, so trade is contested.
Spawns are uneven, so scout to see how close they are.

name: Ancient Spires
summary: Large rock spires and several ponds create choke points that are easy to wall.
tips: Wall the chokes for a safe boom.
Ponds are small; a dock is mostly for fishing boats.
Sacred sites are between the players.

name: Cliffside
summary: A zigzag ridge splits the map; all three sacred sites are on top of it.
tips: The ridge holds every sacred site; whoever controls the high ground wins fights there.
Players start fairly close, so expect early contact.
Extra gold supports gold-heavy unit play.

name: Snake River
summary: A Yue Fei's Legacy map with a winding river.
tips: Find the river crossings early; they are the chokes to hold.

name: Wasteland
summary: A big open centre where most fighting happens, with heavily forested, easy-to-wall edges.
tips: Wall the forest edges for safety, then fight in the open middle.
At least one sacred site is usually in the centre.
Relics may hide in the trees around the edge.

name: Highwoods
summary: Players start in clearings surrounded by patches of forest, with many wallable chokes and a hill in the centre with a sacred site.
tips: Lots of chokes make walling and booming strong.
The central hill sacred site is the main fight.
Plenty of wood, so wooden units and walls are cheap.

name: Ocean Gateway
summary: A Dynasties of the East hybrid map with three sacred sites.
tips: Check how much water is near you; a dock can give a strong economy on hybrid maps.

name: Craters
summary: An open map with two craters by each start: one holds a meteorite resource, the other a small pond.
tips: Mongols and Golden Horde can't take stone from the meteorite, which hurts their economy here.
The meteorite crater is usually between or beside players, so it can be contested.
Ponds in steep craters can be hard to dock on.

name: Waterholes
summary: A standard land layout with small lakes between the starts; in 1v1 the only sacred site is in the centre.
tips: The single central sacred site is the 1v1 objective.
The lakes beside you can give fishing income.
Trade posts are in two opposing corners.

name: Archipelago
summary: Islands surrounded by water; in 1v1 each player starts on their own island.
tips: Navy is mandatory: docks early and control the water.
Larger neutral islands hold extra resources; land there once you control the water.

name: Danube River
summary: A U-shaped river with two shallow crossings and a wooden bridge; one sacred site inside the bend, one on high ground.
tips: The wooden bridge can be destroyed, so don't rely on it as your only path.
The land inside the river bend has lots of resources and a sacred site.
The second sacred site is on the elevated area across the river.

name: Migration
summary: You start on a small island with limited resources and a big island in the centre with relics, sacred sites and a trade post.
tips: Your island runs dry fast; plan to land on the centre island.
Three relics are on the centre island; you start with one on yours.
Kelp stealth forests hide ships around the islands.
